title: Vectors Are Not Neutral: Sensitive-Information Inference from Exported LLM Representations in Summarization
abstract: arXiv:2605.26433v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) summarization systems may pass compact vector representations of private inputs to downstream retrieval, monitoring, audit, or analytic workflows. Even when source documents remain access-restricted, derived vectors may be handled under different access controls and still support sensitive-information inference, creating a residual information-disclosure risk. We study this issue in clinical discharge-summary generation as a high-stakes case study, using electronic health record (EHR)-recorded race as a controlled sensitive-label audit. We audit two artifacts that a system might retain or expose to downstream components: the final prompt-token hidden state and the mean-pooled prompt representation. Our results show that reducing recoverability of the case-study sensitive label from one exported artifact does not necessarily reduce recoverability from another. As a mitigation case study, we introduce Surface

translated_title: 向量并非中立：从大语言模型摘要导出的表示中推断敏感信息
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）摘要系统可能会将私有输入的紧凑向量表示传递给下游的检索、监控、审计或分析工作流。即使源文档仍受访问限制，这些导出的向量可能在不同的访问控制下被处理，却仍然能够支持敏感信息推断，从而带来残余的信息泄露风险。我们在临床出院小结生成这一高风险场景中以案例研究的方式考察该问题，并将电子健康记录（EHR）中记录的种族作为受控的敏感标签进行审计。我们审计了系统可能保留或暴露给下游组件的两种产物：最终的提示词token隐藏状态和平均池化的提示表示。结果表明，降低某一导出产物中敏感标签的可恢复性，并不必然降低另一产物中的可恢复性。作为缓解措施的案例研究，我们提出了Surface（原文摘要在此处截断，后续内容缺失）。
tldr: 该论文以临床出院摘要为案例，首次揭示LLM导出的向量表示（如提示token隐藏状态和平均池化表示）即使脱离源文档的访问控制，仍可被用于推断敏感属性（如患者种族），且针对单一产物的保护措施并不必然对其他产物有效。
en_tdlr: This paper shows, through a clinical discharge-summary case study, that exported LLM vector representations (e.g., final prompt-token hidden states and mean-pooled prompt representations) can leak sensitive attributes such as patient race even when handled under different access controls than the source documents, and that mitigating one artifact does not necessarily reduce recoverability from another.
